subject: Mathematics
learning_objective: Students will identify factor pairs of quadratic expressions (x² + bx + c) and apply correct factoring techniques.
explanation: Factoring a quadratic expression involves finding two linear expressions whose product equals the original quadratic expression. For x² + bx + c, we search for factor pairs (p, q) of c such that p + q = b.

common_misconceptions.name: Incorrect factor-pair selection
common_misconceptions.description: Student selects factors of c that multiply to c but fail to sum to b (e.g., choosing 1 and 6 instead of 2 and 3 for x² + 5x + 6).
common_misconceptions.remediation: Construct a systematic table listing all factor pairs of c with their corresponding sums.

common_misconceptions.name: Difference of squares confusion
common_misconceptions.description: Student treats a difference of squares x² - a² as a perfect square trinomial (x - a)².
common_misconceptions.remediation: Emphasize that the middle x term has a coefficient of 0: x² + 0x - a² = (x + a)(x - a).

worked_example:
Problem: Factor x² + 7x + 12.
Step 1: Identify c = 12, b = 7.
Step 2: List factor pairs of 12:
  - 1 x 12 (sum = 13)
  - 2 x 6  (sum = 8)
  - 3 x 4  (sum = 7) -> MATCH!
Step 3: Write factors as (x + 3)(x + 4).
citations: National Council of Teachers of Mathematics (NCTM) Algebra Standards
